concepts.def: Of the reign of James I (1603-1625)
Society where men hold most authority
Mirrored arrangement of events around a centre
A flawed protagonist who acts immorally
Belief events are pre-decided by fate
The power to choose one's own actions

walkthroughs.body_html:
James I claimed descent from Banquo. The witches' vision of 'a show of eight kings' literally puts James's ancestors on stage.

Macbeth flatters its patron while staging Catholic plotting (Gunpowder, 1605) as ungodly chaos.

The play repeatedly equates power with masculinity.

Lady Macbeth must 'unsex' herself; Macbeth doubts himself when called less than a man; the witches are 'bearded' women. Shakespeare interrogates the patriarchy by showing how brittle its definitions are.

Did the witches cause Macbeth's fall, or merely predict it?

Banquo hears the same prophecy and does nothing. Macbeth's choices are his — so the tragedy is one of free will abused, not determinism. The witches are mirrors, not puppeteers.
